You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Palantir Q2 2026 Earnings Highlights: U.S. Commercial Revenue Surges 149% Year-over-Year Far Above Expectations, Full-Year Revenue Guidance Raised Significantly to $8.150–$8.158 Billion, AI Sovereignty Narrative Strongly Underpins Outlook

TEXT:
Core View
Palantir Technologies ( PLTR ) reported second-quarter 2026 results (ended June 30, 2026) with revenue growing 93% year-over-year to $1.935 billion, significantly beating the market expectation of approximately $1.81 billion. Ad just ed EPS came in at $0.41, above the consensus of $0.35. U.S. commercial revenue soared 149% year-over-year to $764 million, emerging as the standout highlight. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance substantially to $8.150–$8.158 billion (implying roughly 82% year-over-year growth) and lifted U.S. commercial revenue guidance to more than $3.424 billion (at least 134% growth). CEO Alex Karp described the quarter as “otherworldly,” attributing the strength to robust customer demand for “AI sovereignty.” Shares jumped approximately 13–14% in after-hours trading following the release. The results effectively eased investor concerns about large language model substitution and foreign governments shifting toward domestic suppliers.
Detailed Breakdown
Overall Revenue and Profitability Performance
Quarterly revenue reached $1.935 billion, up 93% year-over-year and 19% quarter-over-quarter, well above the analyst expectation of about $1.81 billion.
Adjusted EPS was $0.41, beating the consensus of $0.35.
U.S. revenue totaled $1.573 billion, up 115% year-over-year and 23% quarter-over-quarter.
Adjusted operating income was $1.194 billion, representing a 62% margin; GAAP operating income was $912 million, or a 47% margin.
GAAP net income reached $1.062 billion, equating to a 55% margin and up 225% year-over-year.
Cash from operations was $1.216 billion, or a 63% margin.
Rule of 40 score hit 155%.
The company reaffirmed that it expects to deliver GAAP operating income and net income in every quarter of 2026.
U.S. Commercial Business Performance
U.S. commercial revenue was $764 million, up 149% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter, substantially exceeding the analyst average estimate of approximately $716.4 million. CEO Karp called the figure “staggering.”
U.S. commercial total contract value (TCV) hit a record $2.132 billion, up 153% year-over-year.
U.S. commercial remaining deal value (RDV) stood at $6.238 billion, up 124% year-over-year and 27% quarter-over-quarter.
Key drivers: Strong customer demand for AI sovereignty, with enterprises unwilling to hand over core data and decision-making intelligence to large language model labs. The business is compounding at an unprecedented rate and scale, while the sales headcount remains relatively lean.
Full-year U.S. commercial revenue guidance was raised to in excess of $3.424 billion, representing growth of at least 134% (previous guidance was approximately $3.224 billion).
Other Business Segment Performance
U.S. government revenue reached $809 million, up 90% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter. Overall U.S. operations remained robust.
International revenue was approximately $362.5 million, up 33% year-over-year, notably lagging domestic growth.
Relative weakness overseas stemmed partly from geopolitical pressures: Officials in France and the United Kingdom have recently pushed to terminate partnerships with Palantir in favor of supporting domestic technology firms to safeguard national tech sovereignty.
Contract metrics: Closed 220 deals of at least $1 million, 98 deals of at least $5 million, and 73 deals of at least $10 million. Total TCV was $3.373 billion, up 49% year-over-year.
Full-Year Guidance and Outlook
Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $8.150–$8.158 billion (prior upper end was approximately $7.662 billion), well above the prior analyst consensus of around $7.7 billion, implying roughly 82% year-over-year growth.
Full-year adjusted operating income guidance was lifted to $4.889–$4.897 billion.
Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to $4.5–$4.7 billion.
U.S. commercial revenue guidance for the year was increased to more than $3.424 billion (at least +134%).
Core narrative: Demand for AI sovereignty has been unleashed. Palantir emphasizes customers’ desire for control over data, the prompts fed into models, and organizational/business intelligence (their “alpha”), refusing to become vassals of language model laboratories.
Next-Quarter (Q3 2026) Guidance
Revenue is expected in the range of $2.160–$2.164 billion (above the analyst average expectation of approximately $2.0 billion).
Adjusted operating income is guided to $1.292–$1.296 billion.
Market Backdrop and Investor Concerns
Prior key investor concerns included whether AI developers such as Anthropic building their own software would erode Palantir’s market share, and whether non-U.S. governments would accelerate shifts toward domestic technology providers. The explosive U.S. commercial growth and raised guidance in this quarter helped alleviate some of those worries.
In his shareholder letter, Karp rebutted the large language model substitution thesis, noting that customers do not want models “loose within their homes.” The contest is over control of data, prompts, and organizational intelligence; the company is paid based on value created rather than tokens or usage.
U.S. defense positioning continues to deepen (including collaboration with Anduril on related programs).
Investor reaction was strongly positive: Shares rose approximately 13–14% in after-hours trading and extended gains in overnight sessions. While the U.S. commercial business is “on fire,” management still views it as nascent.
